rows.subtype: Caring for a sick loved one [Response]
rows.description: A caregiver keeps fluids, rest and reassurance in view, watches for danger signs and calls a doctor when worried. They also accept that a sick person may be grumpy without it being personal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: affection, anger, anxiety

rows.description: A child beginning puberty may feel embarrassed, moody and suddenly self-conscious about their body. Without warning, a growing body can feel like a stranger, and honest simple explanations reduce shame.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: anger, shame, embarrassment

rows.description: A parent who talks about periods, voice changes or body hair before they happen, in plain and unhurried words, gives a child confidence. Silence and giggling leave children to learn from rumour and fear.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17
related mind states: amusement, fear, calm

rows.description: A teenager's feelings can swing from delight to despair within hours as hormones and a still-maturing brain interact. The intensity is real, even when the trigger looks small to adults.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: joy

rows.description: A parent whose child suddenly wants privacy, rolls eyes and slams doors may feel rejected. Much of this is normal separation, and staying available without pressure keeps the door open.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: hurt

rows.description: A teenager who matures much earlier or later than classmates may feel awkward, teased or left out. Reassurance that timing varies normally, and that worth is not measured by body, helps.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: embarrassment

rows.description: A teacher sees a formerly cheerful student turn withdrawn, sensitive to teasing or restless. Patience and privacy help, and prolonged sadness, isolation or hopelessness deserve a gentle conversation with family or a counsellor.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: joy, sadness, hope, boredom

rows.description: A teenager experiences sudden crushes, curiosity and confusing physical sensations alongside fear of judgment. Respectful, factual guidance and a trusted adult help them make careful decisions rather than secretive ones.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: admiration, fear, curiosity, confusion

rows.description: A teenager learns that big feelings pass, and finds outlets such as sport, music, writing or talking to a trusted person. Waiting an hour before sending a message or slamming a door prevents many regrets.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12
related mind states: trust, regret

rows.subtopic: Menstrual cycle effects on mood and coping
rows.subtype: First period and feelings about it [Actor]
rows.description: A girl with her first period may feel nervous, proud, embarrassed or confused, sometimes all at once. Clear information, supplies at hand and a calm adult make the experience an ordinary part of growing up.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anxiety, embarrassment, confusion, pride
